description: The Global Coal Terminals Tracker from Global Energy Monitor (GEM), a non-profit research organisation, is a data set of import, export and domestic coal terminals worldwide that move coal between rail, road and shipping. On 26 September 2026 the page counted 522 terminals with 6.2 billion tonnes of operating capacity in 46 countries at more than 200 port locations. Records give terminal capacity, type, location, ownership and development status, including cancelled and paused projects. The latest release was January 2024. Coverage is global. Access is through a free online tracker map, dashboards and summary tables, and the full data set is a spreadsheet downloadable through a short download form on GEM's site, under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the data were last released in January 2024, so recent changes may be missing. Simulation uses are coal supply chain and port disruption studies and exposure of coastal terminals to storms and sea level rise. Related records: data-gem-global-integrated-power-tracker combines GEM's power trackers and data-gem-global-energy-ownership-tracker maps owners.
